steps.instruction: Select an object. In the Properties panel on the right, find the Transform section.
steps.spoken: Click an object. Then look at the panel on the right for the section called Transform.
steps.why: Transform holds the position, turning and size of the selected object.
steps.hint_if_stuck: Click the orange square icon in the Properties panel if you do not see Transform.

steps.instruction: Find Location. It tells you where the object is.
steps.spoken: Location tells you where the object is. X is left and right, Y is forward and back, Z is up and down.
steps.why: Three numbers are enough to place anything in 3D space.
steps.hint_if_stuck: Location is the first group of three boxes under Transform.

steps.instruction: Find Rotation. It tells you how the object is turned.
steps.spoken: Rotation shows how much the object is turned, in degrees.
steps.why: A turn around each of the three directions can point an object anywhere.
steps.hint_if_stuck: Rotation is the second group, below Location.

steps.instruction: Find Scale. A value of 1 means normal size.
steps.spoken: Scale shows the size. One means normal. Two means twice as big.
steps.why: Changing scale stretches the object, like pulling a rubber band.
steps.hint_if_stuck: Scale is the third group, below Rotation.
